key_insight: Task-aware imputation—optimized for the downstream prediction task rather than reconstruction alone—can substantially improve robustness when missing-data patterns differ between training and test time.
engineering_relevance: For deployed ML systems on tabular data, choosing imputation methods should be driven by predictive utility under expected missingness shifts, not by low reconstruction error.
method: Unified task-conditioned optimization treats missing entries as variables tied to the prediction objective.
Two instantiations: an amortized model for missing data at train and test time, and a latent optimization method for incomplete training data only.
Designed to handle train-test mismatches in missingness mechanisms or rates.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 98 tabular datasets, with robustness under train-test mismatch tested on 36 datasets; reconstruction error showed weak correlation with predictive utility (Spearman rho ≈ 0.16–0.32), and task-aware methods achieved win rates up to 80% in hard mismatch settings.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on the availability of task labels and on the specific mismatch regime, so deployment should validate performance under the target missingness pattern.
paper_title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch
